## Distribution of dependent variable (housing price)
```{r}
options(scipen=100)

ggplot(data, aes(x = Price)) + 
  geom_histogram(color="darkslateblue", fill="darkslategray3", bins=50) +
  labs(title="Histogram Distribution of Housing Prices in New York", x="Housing Price", y="Frequency") +
  geom_vline(aes(xintercept=mean(Price)), colour="red") +
   geom_vline(aes(xintercept=median(Price)), colour="deeppink") +
  annotate("label", 
           x=mean(data$Price), 
           y=230, 
           label="Mean",
           fill = "red", color = 'white',
           size = 3.5) +
  annotate("label", 
           x=median(data$Price), 
           y=215, 
           label="Median",  
           fill = "deeppink", color = 'white',
           size = 3.5) 


```

## Boxplot of dependent variable
```{r, fig.width=10, fig.height=6}

Q1 <- quantile(data$Price, 0.25)
Q3 <- quantile(data$Price, 0.75)
median <- median(data$Price)

ggplot(data, aes(x = Price)) + 
  geom_boxplot(color="darkslateblue", fill="darkslategray3", 
               outlier.color="red") +
  labs(title="Boxplot Distribution of Housing Prices in New York") +
    annotate("label", 
           x=median,
           y=0.37, 
           label=paste(round(median)),
           fill = "darkslateblue", color = 'white',
           size = 3.5) +
    annotate("label", 
           x=Q1, 
           y=0, 
           label=paste(round(Q1)),
           fill = "darkslateblue", color = 'white',
           size = 3.5) +
    annotate("label", 
           x=Q3, 
           y=0, 
           label= paste(round(Q3)),
           fill = "darkslateblue", color = 'white',
           size = 3.5) 

```
# Predictor Variables and Dependent Variable
## Land Value
```{r}
# Land.Value
LVmodel <- lm(Price ~ Land.Value, data = data)
LVsummary <- summary(LVmodel)
LVr2 <- LVsummary$r.squared

cor <- cor(data$Land.Value, data$Price)

ggplot(data, aes(x=Land.Value, y=Price)) +
  geom_point(color="darkslateblue", alpha=0.4) +
  geom_smooth(method="lm", color="red") +
  xlim(0, 120000) +
  labs(title = "Scatter Plot of Land Value and Housing Price",
       x="Land Value") +
    annotate("label", 
           x=100000, 
           y=700000, 
           label=paste("Correlation coefficient:", round(cor, 2)),
           fill = "red", color = 'white',
           size = 3.5)


```

LVsummary

## Heat Type
```{r, fig.width=10, fig.height=6}
heat_medians <- data %>% 
  group_by(Heat.Type) %>% 
  summarise(medians = median(Price, na.rm=TRUE))

ggplot(data, aes(x=Heat.Type, y=Price, color=Heat.Type)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  scale_color_brewer(palette = "Spectral") +
  labs(title="Boxplots of Housing Price by Heat Type",
       x="Heat Type",
       y="Housing Price") +
  geom_label(data = heat_medians, 
             aes(x=Heat.Type, y=medians, label=round(medians), color=Heat.Type), 
             size = 3.5) 
```

## QQ plots of Housing Price variable & log(Housing Price)
```{r}
qqnorm(data$Price, main = "QQ Plot of Price"); qqline(data$Price, col = "red")

qqnorm(log(data$Price), main = "QQ Plot of log(Price)"); qqline(log(data$Price), col = "red")
```
## Shapiro Wilk tests
```{r}
library(gt)

# Run tests
test1 <- shapiro.test(data$Price)
test2 <- shapiro.test(log(data$Price))

# Create data frame of results
results <- data.frame(
  Variable = c("Price", "Log(Price)"),
  W = c(round(test1$statistic, 3), round(test2$statistic, 3)),
  Pvalue = c(format.pval(test1$p.value, digits = 3), format.pval(test2$p.value, digits = 3))
)

# Create gt table
results %>%
  gt() %>%
  tab_header(
    title = "Shapiro-Wilk Normality Test"
  )
```
